memories.content: The user keeps the shared laundry-room access card in an entrance drawer.
The user went downstairs 25 minutes after the laundry finished and received a note from another household.
For the next load, the user set a reminder five minutes before the end and removed the laundry immediately.
The user washed light-colored clothes with new jeans, and color transferred onto white socks.
The user later washed the new jeans separately, and the color of the other clothes did not change.
On a day the user did not check the dryer filter, the clothes needed another drying cycle.
On the next use, after emptying the filter, the user finished drying in one cycle.
The building manager judges that not leaving finished laundry for a long time is fair to other households.
When creating a shared laundry-room reminder, base it on the end time of the machine the user started.
Even if the local agent knows where the card is kept, it cannot know which machines in the shared laundry room are currently available.
The user keeps basic repair tools in a box beneath the sink.
On a day the faucet leaked, the user placed only a towel beneath it, and the floor became wet as well.
After sending a photo to building management, the user finalized the time for a repair visit.
Before the technician's visit, the user emptied the area beneath the sink so work could begin immediately.
On a day the user wrote the visit time only in the calendar and turned off the reminder, they heard the doorbell late.
For the next visit, the user enabled a reminder 30 minutes beforehand and answered immediately at the entrance.
After the repair, the user called their maternal aunt to confirm that the spare key entrusted to her was still there.
The user's maternal aunt considers it unsafe to hand the spare key to a repair technician without the user's explicit request.
Obtain the user's reconfirmation before scheduling an external worker to enter the residential unit.
A multi-unit residential building's repair schedule may change because of emergency work or parts availability.

analysis.overview: Both frames show event-timed reminders improving prompt action, with different lead times for laundry completion and repair visits. Otherwise, each frame contributes independent operational knowledge: laundry access, handling, and machine use on one side, and leak response, repair coordination, and residential access safeguards on the other.

relations.reason: The operational pattern is shared, while the explicit event type explains why the reminder basis and lead time differ.
relations.summary: Event-timed reminders improve prompt responses, with a five-minute lead for laundry completion and a 30-minute lead for repair visits.

reports.compared_only: The repair frame covers tool storage, leak containment, management coordination, workspace preparation, spare-key custody, worker-entry authorization, and schedule uncertainty.
reports.differences: Reminders are tied to the relevant event, but laundry pickup uses the machine’s end time and a five-minute lead, while repair attendance uses a 30-minute warning before the visit.
reports.reference_only: The laundry frame covers card location, prompt-pickup fairness, color-transfer prevention, dryer-filter efficiency, and lack of live machine-availability knowledge.
